rationale: C13 is the strongest reusable template because it is likewise a presidential letter transmitting or assigning an earlier foreign-economic-policy report to the chairman of an advisory body, characterizing the report as a contribution, and asking that body to consider it within a broader review of foreign economic policy. C05 is closely connected to the child's specific commission and its comprehensive foreign-economic-policy canvass, but it chiefly establishes the commission's mission rather than supplying the child's report-transmittal form. C08 has a similar report-to-chairman transmittal structure but concerns an unrelated subject and uses more generic administrative language.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am transmitting herewith the report of the Lewis Douglas mission
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Mr. Gray has now submitted his report.
shared_material.explanation: Both letters place an already completed analytical report before the chairman of a policy-review body.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The analysis and findings of the Douglas report represent, in my opinion, a real contribution to thinking in the field of dollar-sterling relationships.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Mr. Gordon Gray made a significant contribution in his study of foreign economic policies in 1950.
shared_material.explanation: Both characterize a named report as a contribution to foreign-economic-policy analysis.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I commend the report to the earnest attention of you and your associates as you undertake your canvass of the whole broad field of foreign economic policy.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: You will wish to formulate your recommendations in the light of the Gray Report's comprehensive analysis of our entire foreign economic policy.
shared_material.explanation: The operative machinery is substantially parallel: an advisory body's broader foreign-economic-policy review is directed to use a transmitted comprehensive report as an input.
